course_name_original: Elasticidad y ampliación de resistencia de materiales (106521)
course_name_en: Elasticity and Advanced Strength of Materials
prerequisites: Students must master certain specific mathematical and physical knowledge (Statics), so it is recommended not to enroll without having completed the subjects in which these are taught with minimal proficiency.

learning_outcomes.text: To provide the tools that allow understanding and identifying the types of stresses that can occur in constructive, structural or mechanical elements.
To evaluate the stresses and deformations that elements can reach.
To begin comparatively weighing the values obtained through these calculations with the limit values established by contrasted previous experience (relevant regulations) or practically acquired.
To define constructive sections and predetermine the internal equilibrium conditions that the materials will support.
Analyze the state of stresses and deformations at a point in a continuous medium.
Know and apply the relationships between stresses and deformations of a solid.
Characterize the load states and types of forces in mechanical prisms.
Provide methods for analyzing the stresses and deformations generated by load states.
Provide tools to dimension different simple elements (beams, supports, cables, shafts, etc.) for strength and rigidity.
Understanding and interpretation of texts and data, development of skills for their concretization and their clear and succinct exposition.
Aptitude for the distribution of resources and time and their implementation in real situations.
Ability to use scientific-technical tools for solving calculation and design problems in Industrial Engineering and aptitude for seeking sustainable engineering solutions.
Ability to work together and ability to develop multidisciplinary projects.
Knowledge and abilities to apply the fundamentals of elasticity and strength of materials to the behavior of real solids.

syllabus_topics: Continuous Media Characteristics: Concept of material point and continuous medium. Characterization of a continuous medium. Continuity equation. Finite transformation of a continuous medium. Interpretation of transformation tensor terms. Infinitesimal transformations. Kinematics of continuous media.

Stress Analysis: Introduction. State of stress. Internal equilibrium of solids. Stress at a point in a given direction. Properties of the stress tensor. Maximum stresses. Stress ellipsoid. Graphical method for stress calculation. Intrinsic components. Stresses in a two-dimensional solid.

Deformations: Introduction. Deformation of an elastic solid. Analysis of the displacement matrix. Rotation matrix. Deformation matrix. Unit deformation in any direction. Deformation ellipsoid. Angular deformations. Planar graphical representation of intrinsic components of the unit deformation vector. Deformations in a two-dimensional solid.
Relationship between Stresses and Deformations: Introduction. Hooke's Law. Transverse deformations. Generalized Hooke's Laws. Lamé's equations.
General Equilibrium State of a Solid: Introduction. Navier's equations. Solutions to the fundamental equation of elasticity. Compatibility equations as a function of stresses.
Compound Stresses: Review of forces. Combination of forces. Compound bending. Eccentric tension (compression). Bending and buckling. Bending and torsion. Solved exercises.

Beams: Introduction. Typical beam sections. Distribution of bending moments in a beam. Statically determined beams supported at two points. Beams fixed at one end and free at the other. Composite section beams. Reinforced beams. Curved beams: stress distribution. Rectangular section curved beams. Trapezoidal section curved beams. T-shaped and I-shaped section curved beams. Deformation in curved bars. Application for calculating horizontal thrusts of arches. Calculation examples in mechanical parts.

Buckling: Introduction. Slender bars. Observations on Euler's formulas. Calculation method based on the CTE (Technical Building Code). Sizing of simple uniform section steel parts. Sizing of composite uniform section steel parts. Calculation of battens in a composite section. Calculation of triangular trusses. Buckling lengths in special cases.
Hyperstatic Beams: General problem. Application examples of the superposition method. Single-span hyperstatic beams. Theorem of three moments. Application examples of the theorem of three moments.
Individual work corrected in class or seminars.
teaching_methods: Practical classes with exercise solving on the whiteboard with student participation

assessment_methods.method: Continuous assessment (includes collected exercises, practical exercises, and attendance)

assessment_rules: The continuous assessment accounts for 35% of the final grade. The final exam consists of four exercises totaling 10 points, where the student must obtain at least 5 points to pass the subject, contributing 65% to the final grade. The continuous assessment grade may be considered for a resit exam. Exceptionally, and if indicated by the student within the first four weeks, part of the continuous assessment may be compensated with exercises and tutoring follow-up.
